files.notes/close_checklist.md:
# June 2026 close — controller checklist

Owner: G. Castellano. Complete in sequence; initial support before moving on.

1. Reconcile operating cash to the June bank statement. For every book-side item identified by the reconciliation, prepare one correcting journal entry per item.
2. Review the payroll register for any pay period ending after 6/30 that pays in July; some months all runs pay in-month. If such a period exists, accrue the full gross wages to Accrued Liabilities.
3. Confirm June prepaid amortization against the prepaid schedule, contracts, and GL. If it is not already posted, book June prepaid amortization as ONE combined journal entry—do not duplicate an existing entry. Take a full month of amortization in the month an item begins.
4. Check the GL, then book June depreciation per the fixed asset register.
5. Compare June vendor-bill documents with GL coding. Verify that each expense account is correct and reclass anything miscoded.
6. After items 1-5 are posted, prepare June budget-vs-actual variance commentary on an as-closed basis.
files.notes/company_background.md:
# Company background

Juniper Goods Co. began in 2021 when its founder, an enthusiastic home organizer and habitual gift-basket maker, noticed how difficult it was to find useful household goods that also felt warm, durable, and presentable. What started as a carefully edited online storefront grew through repeat customers, word of mouth, and a knack for pairing practical products with straightforward guidance.

Today, Juniper Goods Co. sells home, desk, pantry, and everyday gift items through its ecommerce site. The assortment favors uncomplicated design, reliable materials, and products that can move easily from personal use to business gifting. The team keeps the catalog intentionally selective rather than trying to stock every possible variation.

The company has a small, hands-on crew spanning merchandising, customer care, fulfillment, marketing, and finance. Their working style is informal but conscientious: product samples circulate around the office, customer notes are read aloud, and operational fixes tend to begin as quick conversations before becoming written procedures.

The current focus is steady improvement. Juniper Goods Co. is refining its product pages, tightening inventory routines, building stronger vendor relationships, and making month-end processes more consistent. The business remains an ordinary going concern, serving its existing customer base while testing measured ways to broaden its reach.
files.notes/marketing_plan_h2.md:
# H2 marketing plan — working draft

## Direction

Keep Juniper Goods Co. recognizable while sharpening the brand voice: useful, warm, and pleasantly unfussy. The refresh should improve consistency across product pages, email, paid media, packaging inserts, and partner materials without making the company feel overly polished.

## Priorities

- Refresh core brand language and create a practical messaging guide for the team.
- Improve product storytelling around materials, use cases, care, and gifting.
- Run two educational webinars per quarter, using topics that naturally connect to home organization, thoughtful gifting, and everyday workspaces.
- Pilot partner co-marketing with a complementary brand. Keep the first collaboration narrow enough to evaluate audience fit and operating effort.
- Build reusable creative from customer questions, product demonstrations, and behind-the-scenes fulfillment content.
- Coordinate email and paid-media themes so customers encounter one clear campaign story at a time.

## Measurement

Review engagement quality, repeat visits, email response, partner-referred traffic, and product-page behavior. Separate short campaign observations from broader brand conclusions.

## Open items

Confirm campaign ownership, webinar speakers, partner shortlist, creative capacity, and channel mix after the Q2 close. Document lessons at each quarter-end and carry only the strongest tests forward.
files.notes/prior_accountant_memo.md:
# Notes from your chatty predecessor

For G. Castellano — a few things I learned the hard way:

- Check the tail end of the bank statement carefully. The bank's own service fees and other charges usually appear near statement end, and we have historically booked them during close rather than earlier in the month.
- June got busy, so do not assume the vendor-bill expense coding is right. Compare the entries to the source documents in `bills/`; those documents are authoritative, and anything inconsistent should be corrected.
- The Q2 budget was locked in early April. The one-off items that arrived in June were never included in the plan, so they are the reason several of the large variances show up.
- Payroll timing matters this month: the back half of June pays in early July. The payroll register contains the relevant dates, so use it when preparing the accrual.
